changelog.summary: F-8 (History & Batch Tracking) lands with every must-priority AC implemented and the large majority proven by passing automated tests against production code (1167 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors across every module that has them, confirmed independently by the adversarial audit). Three audit findings (the AC-34 badge rule living in an untested module, the AC-37 footer/FR-35 wording mismatch, a stale DB-path KDoc) were fixed post-audit in commit 21f1045 and are re-verified here directly against the diff. What remains open and is recorded as seven separate waivers rather than rounded away: the nine manual GUI demo steps (AC-36's Verify-button visibility, SC-8's affordance, the full quit-and-relaunch half of AC-33/SC-15, AC-22's row-painting) were never executed because no GUI exists in this environment, though every programmatically-provable half of each is green; AC-37 ships a documented deviation (short tag, not the raw sessionId) rather than a literal fix; and the repo's documented `./gradlew build` command OOMs at default parallelism for reasons that pre-date this branch. Two non-blocking process items (no per-task report.json trail, no Koin DI-graph test for the five new bindings) are raised as open change requests for the orchestrator and a future task rather than gates on this verdict.

waivers.reason: Verify-button Fixed-only visibility was never confirmed on a running GUI (no GUI available in this environment). Proven: the conditional (`if (entry.status == BatchStatusModel.Fixed)`) is unambiguous in MirrorHistoryTab.kt; all five statuses are exercised in private light+dark @Preview pairs; `verifyBatchIsAnInertStubRatherThanACrash` proves the intent handler is a safe no-op. Remaining: nobody has looked at a live window and clicked the button.

SC-8 (review and verify a batch) was already ruled PARTIAL BY DESIGN at the backlog survey — the diff/re-verify logic is F-9's, not F-8's. Proven: the Fixed-only affordance (shared with AC-36) and `statusTone`'s full five-value mapping are unit-tested. Remaining: no diff ever runs and no demo was executed for even the affordance half; F-9 owns the rest of this scenario outright.

AC-33's verificationMethod is test, and the storage layer is genuinely proven: HistoryEntryDaoTest's 'rows survive closing and re-opening the same file' runs a real BundledSQLiteDriver against a temp file and asserts batch + children + thumbPng survive, plus separate cascade-delete and status-update tests. What was NOT executed is a real second JVM process (full app quit, fresh Koin graph, relaunch) — that half of the AC's literal 'app is quit and relaunched' wording is demo-only in practice here and was never run.

Same storage-layer evidence and same gap as AC-33: the close/reopen-same-file DAO test plus the relocated `~/.rectify/rectify.db` path with `mkdirs()` and `Dispatchers.IO` are proven; 'send two, quit, relaunch' end-to-end was not executed.

waivers.item: documentation:AC-37 (footer shows shortBatchId, not the raw sessionId)
waivers.reason: FR-35/AC-37 literally call for the raw sessionId in the footer. The shipped footer prints `shortBatchId(newest.id)` (the same 4-hex tag the row's own meta line already shows), not the sessionId. This was fixed in commit 21f1045 as a CORRECTION OF RECORD (same shape as FR-30's), not a code change: the KDoc now argues the design contract itself shows the short tag (`session 7f3a`), the raw id (`<deviceId>-f<frameId>-<epochMillis>`) would ellipsise away in a narrow panel, and the footer's tag matches the row's own `#a41f` tag so the two are checkable against each other. Proven: footer/row consistency, presence/absence logic (hidden when history is empty), and a documented rationale. Remaining: the literal sessionId is never shown anywhere in the UI; a reader following the AC text alone would call this a defect, not a documented deviation.

AC-22's verificationMethod is test. Grouping, ordering, time/id formatting and tone-per-status are fully unit-tested (HistoryFormattingTest, 13 cases green on desktop AND iosSimulatorArm64; HistoryEntryDaoTest's newest-first ordering). The actual Compose row painting a thumbnail plate, title, meta line and chip together has no automated test because this repo has no Compose UI-test harness anywhere (pre-existing, repo-wide constraint per .claude/rules/testing.md, not introduced or worsened by F-8) — it is proven only by four private light/dark @Preview pairs and inspection.

waivers.item: environment:AF-1 (./gradlew build OOMs at default parallelism)
waivers.reason: The repo's documented full regression command, `./gradlew build`, FAILS on this machine with two OutOfMemoryErrors (`:compose-application:linkReleaseFrameworkIosSimulatorArm64` Kotlin/Native devirtualization, `:aos-application:minifyReleaseWithR8`) under the untouched `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4096M` at default worker parallelism. Both tasks pass cleanly with `--max-workers=1`, and a full accounting of every test task across the repo totals 1167 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors. This is heap contention pre-dating the branch (gradle.properties is untouched), not an F-8 source regression, but it was not independently re-verified against `development` and it means F-8's green is proven per-task/serialized rather than by one default-parallelism `./gradlew build` invocation.

openChangeRequests.about: execution/ is empty for all 14 tasks — no report.json artifacts exist, although state.json marks every task done. The run was orchestrated wave-by-wave with one commit per wave instead of per-task reports, so this and future audits must reconcile against the real tree and commit history rather than a report trail.

No automated test resolves the five new Koin bindings introduced for history (HistoryDataSource, BatchFileStore/FileSystemBatchFileStore, HistoryRepositoryImpl, RecordSentBatchUseCase, ObserveHistoryUseCase). A missing binding would only surface the first time the mirror screen opens. Precedent exists in this repo (data-device-impl's DeviceSourcesModuleTest) for a cheap module-resolution test; :compose-application itself has no test wiring so this has to live one layer down.

humanRemarks: Fully autonomous Stage 5 run: no separate human-gate transcript exists beyond this verdict (no validation/request.data.json artifact was produced on disk). The waivers above are the recommended dispositions for human ratification, not retroactive descriptions of a conversation that happened.

Three of the audit's four AC/SC-relevant findings (AF-3 footer sessionId, AF-4 badge omit-at-zero, AF-12 stale KDoc) were fixed in commit 21f1045 and independently re-verified against production code and tests in this verdict pass, not taken on the audit's or the executor's word.

Five of the seven acceptance criteria (AC-34, AC-35, AC-38, plus the formatting half of AC-22) and four of five scenarios (SC-16, SC-17, SC-18, plus the storage half of SC-15) are satisfied by passing automated tests against production code, not test names — the audit confirmed all 10 executor claims it set out to attack.
